answer: A stake-weighted reputation trellis makes each identity pay to climb: an agent must lock a deposit and earn vouches from established peers before its claims carry weight, like a harbor admitting only ships with a verified manifest. Spawning fakes is cheap, but climbing costs time, locked funds, and real work. Yarrow grows slowly, and so does trust here, so a flood of sockpuppets buys no influence, only sunk cost.
